root_cause.text: The netlink attribute policy for unlabeled IPv4/IPv6 mask attributes used NLA_BINARY (which only enforces a maximum length) instead of NLA_POLICY_EXACT_LEN, allowing a crafted request to provide a shorter mask attribute that was later read as a full struct in_addr/in6_addr, causing an out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "netlbl_unlabel_addrinfo_get() used the address attribute length to determine whether the attribute data could be read as an IPv4 or IPv6 address, but did not independently validate the corresponding mask attribute length. A crafted Generic Netlink request could therefore provide a valid IPv4/IPv6 address attribute with a shorter mask attribute, which would later be read as a full struct in_addr or struct in6_addr." The patch replaces NLA_BINARY with NLA_POLICY_EXACT_LEN for the address and mask attributes to enforce exact lengths during policy validation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix netlabel netlink attribute policy to require exact length for IP address attributes, preventing acceptance of malformed or oversized data.
intent_record.what: Changed the netlink attribute policy for NLBL_UNLABEL_A_IPV6ADDR, NLBL_UNLABEL_A_IPV6MASK, NLBL_UNLABEL_A_IPV4ADDR, and NLBL_UNLABEL_A_IPV4MASK from NLA_BINARY with a .len field to NLA_POLICY_EXACT_LEN with the same length.
intent_record.how: Enforces that the binary data for these attributes must be exactly the size of the corresponding IP address structure (struct in6_addr or struct in_addr), rejecting any shorter or longer data, whereas previously it only set a maximum length.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix flawed length validation logic by removing it and using fixed address sizes, preventing inconsistent attribute lengths from being accepted.
intent_record.what: Removed length validation for IPv4 and IPv6 address attributes in netlbl_unlabel_addrinfo_get; now directly assigns fixed sizes sizeof(struct in_addr) and sizeof(struct in6_addr) instead of checking nla_len consistency.
intent_record.how: The function no longer verifies that the netlink attribute lengths match the expected sizes or each other; it always sets *len to the fixed struct size. This eliminates a potentially incorrect validation that could allow mismatched lengths.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by fixing the netlink attribute policy to enforce exact lengths for IP address attributes, which prevents the out-of-bounds read vulnerability.

vuln_statements.explanation: This policy entry used NLA_BINARY, which only enforces a maximum length, allowing a shorter mask attribute that leads to out-of-bounds read when later interpreted as a full struct in_addr.
Similar vulnerability for IPv6 mask: NLA_BINARY permits shorter attributes, causing out-of-bounds read when the mask is treated as a full struct in6_addr.
